title: Elon Musk on running Twitter: cost cuts, bots, paid verification and free speech (BBC, April 2023)
summary: In a contentious BBC interview six months after taking over Twitter, Musk explains the cash-burn math behind the layoffs, why paid verification is meant to raise the cost of bots and disinformation, and why he favors open algorithms, Community Notes and seeking negative feedback. He also shares his tweeting rules.

principles.text: When cash is about to run out, cut costs immediately; survival outranks how the process feels.
principles.quote: the companies either going to go bankrupt um or if if we do not cut costs immediately um this is not a caring uncaring situation it's like if the whole ship sinks nobody's going to drop

principles.text: Charge for verification mainly to raise the cost of bots and disinformation, not as a giant revenue stream.
principles.quote: what we're what we're really trying to do here with uh verification is to massively raise the cost of disinformation and and bots in general

principles.text: Platforms that don't require paid verification risk being overwhelmed by AI bots.
principles.quote: my prediction is that any social media company that does not uh insist on paid verification will simply be overwhelmed uh by uh Advanced AI Bots

principles.text: Open-source the algorithm so users trust what they can see, and keep improving it from outside feedback.
principles.quote: are you going to trust some sort of blackbox algorithm from some other site or you going to trust the thing that you can actually see and understand

principles.text: Seek negative feedback and don't block critics; losing your feedback loop is dangerous.
principles.quote: if you do lose your Fe Fe back Loop that's that's actually not good um so uh you know if if so I think it is actually important to get negative feedback

principles.text: Before posting anything controversial, save it as a draft and re-read it the next day.
principles.quote: if you're going to Tweet something that uh maybe is controversial uh save it as a draft and look it it the next day and see if you still want to tweet it
